taxonomy:
Below is a practical taxonomy of **grid-based logic games**, with your listed titles grouped by their dominant solving mechanic.

---

# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## 1. Shading / Painting Puzzles
Core action: decide which cells are black/shaded vs white/unshaded.

### 1.1 Illumination-based shading
- **Akari** — place bulbs to illuminate all white cells while respecting numbered black cells.

### 1.2 Binary shading with connectivity / adjacency constraints
- **Heyawake** — shade cells by room counts; black cells cannot touch; white area connected.
- **Hitori** — shade duplicate numbers to remove repeats; black cells non-adjacent; white cells connected.
- **Kurodoko** — shade cells so clue cells “see” a given number of white cells; black cells non-adjacent.
- **Nurikabe** — build white clue-islands of given sizes separated by one connected black wall; no 2×2 black.
- **Usowan** — like a liar/mines-style shading puzzle with one false clue per room; black cells non-adjacent.
- **Yajilin** — shade some cells according to arrow clues while also forming a loop through remaining cells.
- **Nurimisaki** — shade cells so circled cells become promontories; white connected; no 2×2 monochrome blocks.
- **Nurimeizu** — shade whole rooms to create a maze path with shortest-path conditions.
- **Tilepaint** — shade/unshade entire tiles under directional count clues.
- **Sto-stone** — shade cells in rooms with gravity/drop behavior constraints.

### 1.3 Shading with polyomino / shape constraints
- **LITS** — place one tetromino per region; shaded cells connected; same tetromino types cannot touch edgewise.
- **Norinori** — shaded cells must form dominoes; each region contains exactly two shaded cells.
- **Nuritwin** — each region contains two equal-sized shaded blocks; all shaded cells globally connected.
- **Choco Banana** — black connected components must be rectangles; white components must not be rectangles.

### 1.4 Local clue sum / reach shading
- **Kurotto** — circles give the total length of black runs extending orthogonally.
- **Shakashaka** — place triangular half-cell shades so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares.

---

## 2. Loop-Drawing Puzzles
Core action: draw a single closed loop on or through the grid.

### 2.1 Edge-based loop puzzles
- **Slitherlink** — draw a loop along grid edges matching numeric edge counts.
- **Masyu** — loop through black/white pearls with straight/turn constraints.
- **Suraromu** — loop passes through gates in a numbered order from a start circle.

### 2.2 Cell-center loop puzzles
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop passes through cells; white circles in a room are all straight or all turning.
- **Mid-loop** — loop segments must have black circles at their midpoints.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop visits each room once and uses either all moons or all suns in that room.
- **Nagareru** — directed loop with arrow cells and wind constraints.
- **Yajilin** — hybrid: loop through unshaded cells while satisfying arrow clues.
  
---

## 3. Path / Connection Puzzles
Core action: connect endpoints or route paths, not necessarily as a single loop.

### 3.1 Pair-connection path puzzles
- **Numberlink** — connect matching numbers with non-crossing paths.
- **Yosenabe** — move numbered circles into gray areas by straight arrows; sums must match area clues.

### 3.2 Network / graph connection puzzles
- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with 1–2 bridges into one connected network.

### 3.3 Directed movement / relocation puzzles
- **Satogaeri** — move circles across countries by exact distances so each country ends with one circle.
- **Pencils** — identify pencil shapes and draw a path from each tip with length tied to pencil clues.

---

## 4. Region Division / Partition Puzzles
Core action: divide the grid into regions satisfying size/shape/label constraints.

### 4.1 Rectangle partition puzzles
- **Shikaku** — partition into rectangles, each containing one clue equal to its area.

### 4.2 General region-size partition puzzles
- **Five Cells** — divide grid into pentomino-like regions of exactly five cells using border clues.
- **Double Choco** — partition into regions containing matching white/gray shapes.
- **Sashigane** — partition into one-cell-wide L-shaped regions with bend/end clues.

### 4.3 Region filling by equal-number areas
- **Fillomino** — partition into polyominoes whose size equals the number filling them.

---

## 5. Placement / Object-Placement Puzzles
Core action: place discrete objects or marks into cells.

### 5.1 Object placement with visibility / counting
- **Akari** — place bulbs.
- **Hebi** — place snake segments numbered 1–5 with visibility and non-touching constraints.
- **Evolomino** — place squares to form evolving polyomino blocks along arrows.

### 5.2 Symbol placement
- **Juosan** — fill each cell with horizontal or vertical marks under territory and run-length constraints.

---

## 6. Number-Placement Puzzles
Core action: fill cells with numbers under row/column/region constraints.

### 6.1 Latin / room-based number placement
- **Sudoku** — place 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with 1..n; arrow clues indicate local maxima; equal numbers cannot touch across rooms.
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with 1..n; equal numbers in a row/column must be sufficiently separated.

### 6.2 Number packing / fitting
- **Nansuke** — place listed numbers into the grid horizontally or vertically.

### 6.3 Sequence / local-number structure
- **Hebi** — numbered snake sequences.
- **Fillomino** — also fits here as number placement plus region formation.

---

## 7. Hybrid Region-and-Shading Puzzles
These combine region logic with shading strongly enough to merit a cross-category note.

- **Heyawake** — rooms + shading + connectivity.
- **LITS** — rooms + tetromino shading.
- **Norinori** — rooms + domino shading.
- **Nuritwin** — rooms + paired shaded blocks.
- **Tilepaint** — tiles + shading.
- **Sto-stone** — rooms + shading + gravity.
- **Double Choco** — region partition + color-shape matching.

---

## 8. Hybrid Loop-and-Shading / Loop-and-Obstacle Puzzles
- **Yajilin** — loop + black-cell placement.
- **Nagareru** — loop + directional constraints.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop + room-content selection.
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop + roomwise turn/straight classification.

---

# Notes on ambiguous cases
Some of these naturally belong in more than one branch:

- **Akari** is both a placement puzzle and a shading/coverage puzzle.
- **Fillomino** is both number placement and region partition.
- **Yajilin** is fundamentally hybrid: loop + shading.
- **Hebi** mixes placement, sequencing, and visibility.
- **Double Choco** is best seen as a partition puzzle, though color-pattern matching is central.
- **Chained Block** is somewhat unusual; it fits best under **shape/block-formation logic**, adjacent to shading/region puzzles.
